confirmed.title: User #1 signs in on the live site only as 'admin_1' and has no email: the Phase-1 decision that was to precede the switch-on is still open; the beta login fails silently on live, blocks the beta's own sign-in, and the admin's lock has no reset way back
confirmed.where: apps/edge-bff/app/accounts.py:30 and :118-124 (seed_identity); apps/edge-bff/app/main.py:825 (shared SIGNIN_LOGIN counter); apps/edge-bff/app/errors.py:62; EXEC.md:15591-15594; ERRORS_AND_SOLUTIONS.md:10071-10072
confirmed.fix: Put the open Phase-1 decision to the user before the switch-on. (1) The admin's live login: either tell the user it is 'admin_1' and use it in the live smoke, or keep 'edge' with a forward migration that exempts the seed from the reserved-username CHECK and seed_identity. (2) An email for user #1, set by an audited statement, so 'Forgot password?' is its way back. Until then, record that the operator unlock is the admin's only way back on live, and word MFA_LOCKED without the email reset for an account that has no email.
confirmed.verifier:
The core of A1 holds, so it is not refuted. It is low severity, not medium, because most of the aggravating parts are by design or bounded.

What I confirmed with my own run and the records:
- The seed turns EDGE_LOGIN 'edge' into username 'admin_1' with no email. On live, 'edge' with the right password answers 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS; 'admin_1' answers 403 MFA_REQUIRED, the planned admin path.
- The records say the admin's username and email must be decided "before EDGE_MULTIUSER is switched on", and that without it the old login 'edge' does not work at the switch-on (EXEC.md:15591-15594; ERRORS M478, "before Phase 6", which EXEC defines as the switch-on).
- No decision is recorded at 13f40871, and Option A's list of what the user must give (EXEC.md:15992-15995) leaves it out.
- So at the switch-on the user's known login fails with no hint, and user #1 has no self-service recovery on live. That is a real unmet precondition of the switch-on.

What I refute as aggravations:
1. The 401 is the designed answer that does not reveal whether an account exists. The live name is documented (README:897-899, DATABASE_CHANGELOG:136).
2. The shared counter:
   - It is shared by design ("shared by every edge-bff instance", throttle.py:2).
   - It is keyed by the client address, so it blocks only that same address, for at most about 15 minutes (retry_after 917 s).
   - 10 wrong tries on the beta alone give the same 429. A different address still signs in on the beta (200).
   - e2e_dev.py:917-921 targets the beta's own service variables, not live. A live admin needs MFA, which no script can pass, so the smoke-script scenario is speculative.
3. The way back:
   - The operator unlock is documented as "the way back of an admin without an email address, who has no reset" (scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py:6). It was fixed for accounts without an authenticator by C3-18 (M507).
   - In my run, the right password after the unlock gives 403 MFA_REQUIRED, and the beta stays open (200) during the live lock.
   - Re-locking after a way back is a property of the 100-failure cap on every account. An email reset is re-locked by the same 100 tries.
   - 'admin_1' appears in no page or script the site serves.
4. MFA_LOCKED (errors.py:62) also offers "Wait 24 hours" and "an operator can also unlock it", and both are true for user #1. It is reachable only after the right password. Round 2 already listed it as open under M478.

Nothing reaches what it must not and nothing leaks. The fix needs no code before the switch-on: tell the user the live login is admin_1 and put the open decision to them. Keeping 'edge' needs a forward migration; adding an email needs an audited statement. Both can also be done after the switch-on.

confirmed.title: A stranger can still close a locked account's reset: the daily send cap and a code's 5 tries are keyed by the address or code alone; M507 re-keyed only the wrong-code counters
confirmed.where: apps/edge-bff/app/throttle.py:53 (SEND_EMAIL); apps/edge-bff/app/auth_flows.py:173 (_may_send, key = the email) and :220-229 (_check_code: attempts per code); apps/edge-bff/app/accounts.py:47 and :265-282
confirmed.fix: Ask the user whether to accept this with the operator unlock as the way back. If not, the smallest fix is at the reset layer: a stranger's wrong tries must never consume the code the owner's client asked for (keep the tries per code and client, or bind the reset code to the requesting browser with a cookie as registration does), and count reset mails per (address, client) under a higher per-address ceiling. Add the scenario beside test_a_stranger_cannot_close_both_the_sign_in_and_its_way_back.
confirmed.verifier:
Not refuted. I reproduced it at 13f40871 with my own test. M507 re-keyed only the daily wrong-code caps, CODE_ADDRESS and CODE_USER. That fixes C3-17's route of 20 wrong codes, and M507's own test passes on the exported tree. Two counters still decide the way back from the 100-failure lock, and neither is keyed by the client:
- SEND_EMAIL, 10 emails per address per day.
- A code's 5 tries.

So a stranger who knows the login and address can close the reset after the lock, in about 15 requests.

What I ran: the live site in pre-launch mode, a test account marked with its audit row, and Railway's header shape '<ip>, 152.233.40.1'.
1. 100 wrong passwords lock the account, and the owner's right password gets 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS.
2. The stranger presses "Forgot password?" 10 times. The owner's own forgot and its resend then answer 202 and mail nothing for 86409 s.
3. The stranger sends 5 wrong codes, which consumes the 10th code. That code then gets 400 CODE_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED for the owner.
4. Once a lock ends, 10 wrong passwords from one address lock the account again.
5. The operator unlock works, but the stranger locks the account again with 100 requests.

This is not a recorded, informed acceptance:
- Decision 3 "a" of 2026-11-19 (shared emails) was asked with option A saying "the sign-in limit and the account cap no longer lock them out". The 3c refuter showed that this is false and asked for the decision to be put again together with C3-17. The records show no such re-ask.
- The user's "2a" is recorded as "so a stranger's tries do not block the owner's code", and the code does not hold that.

Why medium and not blocker in pre-launch:
- Only the admin and the test accounts can sign in on live, and a stranger must already know their login and address. I found no way to enumerate them.
- With EDGE_EMAIL_MODE=log the operator reads every reset code from the outbox anyway, so the operator is already involved.
- The admin can still sign in on the beta (switch off, no cap).

It becomes high at the launch, when every account is a target.

One correction to the finding: 5 client addresses are enough (2 logins x 10 each), or one address over about 75 minutes.

confirmed.title: The checked commit's CI run is recorded red, and edge-bff-live is to deploy from branch `live` with checkSuites true, so the planned switch-on deployment would very likely not go out (and CONTRACT 17's 'every suite green' rule is not met)
confirmed.where: .railway/railway.ts:270 (declared edge-bff-live source: branch live, checkSuites true); .github/workflows/backend-tests.yml:29-31,65; ERRORS_AND_SOLUTIONS.md M510 (at aee67c30, line 8977)
confirmed.fix: Create `live` at aee67c30, or the newest main whose edge-bff CI run is green: its app and static code equal 13f40871's. Record that the checked app code equals that commit's. Alternatively re-run 13f40871's failed workflow until it is green before connecting the source. Confirm the deployment reaches SUCCESS before touching the beta's EDGE_HOUSEKEEPING_ENABLED.
confirmed.verifier:
Confirmed in substance. Commit 13f40871 has a recorded red Backend tests run. The declared live source is branch `live` with checkSuites true. CONTRACT 17 requires every suite of the pushed version to be green.

Railway's gate on edge-bff really does hold a deploy when a suite is red. It happened before: deployment 655a2e87 was SKIPPED with "CI check suite failed" (M467). So at the switch-on, one of two things happens:
(a) the edge-bff-live deployment is held or skipped, and the plan does not run as written; or
(b) if it goes out anyway, through a manual deploy or a connect-time deploy that ignores the gate, the live site gets a version whose suite is red, which breaks the user's push-to-live rule.

Two parts of the finding are overstated:
- "Very likely": the same test and page code passed at the first try in run 44677001491 (99b5ea20; no Monitor file changed between 99b5ea20 and 13f40871). A fresh run on `live` fails only when the runner's frames are late. Whether Railway also counts main's red suite on the same SHA could not be checked offline.
- The housekeeping scenario: a half-done switch-on happens only if the beta's switch is flipped before live reaches SUCCESS.

Nothing is exposed and it fails closed, but the commit chosen for `live` has to change before the switch-on.

The fix holds: the edge-bff-live build context (rootDirectory /apps/edge-bff) is the same at aee67c30 except one test file. Caveat from my runs: the fixed test's last assertion (line 82 at aee67c30) is still frame-sensitive under the same slow-frame simulation. So read aee67c30's real CI result, or the newest main's, before creating `live`; do not assume it is green.

Confirmed at 13f40871 with my own run. The shell has no way to know which site it is on, and it offers the Monitor to everyone on the live site.

The code:

The server still holds the guarantee: every monitor.* route answers 404 on live, so no AI or data is reachable. The page does not hold the rule the user decided on 2026-11-19 ("4 ok": the whole Monitor tab hidden on live; CONTRACT 8b 3e: "On the live site the Monitor is not offered at all"). The records say the opposite (README:822; the docstring of test_c3c_site_recheck.py:11-12 "so the shell shows no Monitor"; the 3c check record). No test looks at the live rail.

My probe ran on a `git archive` extract of 13f40871 (the served edge-app.js has the same sha256 as the 13f40871 blob), with EDGE_SITE=live, the switch on, pre-launch and guests on:
- **Visitor, desktop:** the rail shows 'EDGE: Monitor', 'Monitor' and 'Research', all visible (`is_visible` true, 40x40 px boxes). Each click goes to /monitor, which shows the sign-in page; in pre-launch a visitor cannot sign in. A reload there shows raw JSON `{"error":{"code":"NOT_FOUND",...}}`.

Nobody reaches anything they must not, no data leaks, and nobody is locked out: the rail's Terminal button and the sign-in page's 'Open the Terminal without an account' link lead back. It is still worth fixing with the switch-on, because it breaks a user-decided rule on every page for every visitor and account, sends the logo and the AI entry points to dead ends, and the fix is small.

confirmed.title: 'Sign out everywhere' and the password change on live do not end user #1's beta sessions, which hold '*', although the dialog says they do
confirmed.where: app/accounts.py:350-356 (revoke_all: WHERE user_id = %s); app/auth_flows.py:735-736 (sign-out-all), :393-394 (change), :359-360 (reset); app/store.py:107-111 (a beta session has user_id NULL and no idle check); static/edge-labels.js:235-237
confirmed.fix: For the seed account (owner_key = EDGE_OWNER, access.seed), revoke_all and the change and reset statements also revoke `edge_bff.sessions WHERE owner_key = <seed owner> AND user_id IS NULL`. Otherwise, reword the dialog for user #1: the beta's sessions and password are not covered, and they end by rotating EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER or by an operator revoke.
confirmed.verifier:
The finding holds at 13f40871. I checked the code and ran a probe against a clean export of the commit.

How the code behaves:
- The beta's sign-in stores a switch-off session row with user_id NULL and owner_key EDGE_OWNER.
- The beta's resolver accepts any such row that is not revoked and has not expired. It checks no idle time, no account status and no identity, and it returns the '*' principal.
- On the live site, the three paths that revoke sessions all filter on `user_id = <account>`, so they never reach user #1's beta rows: sign-out-all (`revoke_all`), the password change and the reset.

This contradicts what the system says it does:
- CONTRACT 12 says "every session of the account, on both sites".
- The R2-20 fix note says "every session, both websites".
- The dialog says "on both EDGE websites, this one included", and after a change it says "EDGE signed out your other devices".
- The comment in edge-labels.js shows the builder assumed that sharing the sessions table was enough.
- The R2-20 test only checks a paid user's switch-on sessions. User #1's beta sessions are never tested.
- No entry in M500-M512 records this.

Who it affects and when:
- Only user #1, the only account that can hold beta sessions. No visitor or other account gains anything.
- It matters during an incident. If the admin ends everything on live after losing a device or suspecting a stolen cookie, a beta session keeps '*' for up to 24 h with no idle timeout. That session reaches the AI, the Monitor with every conversation, the admin routes and point-in-time Flow, all over the same data.
- The beta has no "sign out everywhere" of its own. The account dialog only appears when accounts are on.

One part of the reviewer's scenario is documented behaviour, not a new defect. After a change on live, the beta still accepts the old password without MFA. This follows from the R2-2 rule ("The switch-off sign-in itself still reads EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER", README). It does mean a leaked password also needs EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER rotated, and the page does not say so.

Severity: medium, not a blocker. It is a session-ending control that fails open for the most powerful session, while the page tells the admin it worked. It does not stop the switch-on and does not expose anyone else.

Note: a later commit, 61d9333b (not the checked commit), adds ACCOUNT_SESSIONS (`user_id = X OR (user_id IS NULL AND owner_key = X's owner_key)`) to revoke_all, the reset and the change. I did not test it. If branch `live` is created at 13f40871 as planned, the defect ships.

confirmed.title: The admin's login on the live site is admin_1, not the beta's edge, and user #1 has no email: the switch-on sign-in fails with the usual login and there is no reset path
confirmed.where: app/accounts.py:30, :33, :118-127 (seed_identity: the reserved 'edge' becomes 'admin_1'; email only when the login is an email); app/main.py:834 (find_login by username or email only); records: DATABASE_CHANGELOG.md:136 (dev's seed row: username admin_1, no email), EXEC.md:15591-15594 (open before the switch is turned on), ERRORS_AND_SOLUTIONS.md:10076-10077 ('To be decided before Phase 6'); EXEC.md:15992 (Option A's 'Needed from the user' list leaves it out)
confirmed.fix: Before the switch-on, settle the 2026-11-16 decision with the user: either tell him the live login is admin_1, or let the seed keep 'edge' with a migration. Give user #1 a verified email so the reset path exists. Add both to Option A's 'Needed from the user'.
confirmed.verifier:
The finding holds at 13f40871, but in a narrower form than claimed and at a lower severity.

**What is confirmed**
- `seed_identity` (accounts.py:118-124) turns the reserved `edge` into `admin_1`. `edge` is reserved at accounts.py:30 and by the database CHECK in 20261116_003:42-43. The seed gives an email only when the login is an email.
- The seed never renames or re-mails an existing row (accounts.py:149 and :159). So user #1, shared by both sites, stays `admin_1` with no email (DATABASE_CHANGELOG.md:136).
- The switch-on sign-in looks an account up by username or email only (main.py:834, accounts.py:254-263).
- Forgot password and reset need an active account with that email (auth_flows.py:313-327, :352).
- A precondition recorded on 2026-11-16 is still open: decide the admin's username and add an email before EDGE_MULTIUSER is turned on (EXEC.md:15591-15594; ERRORS:10071-10072). README:886 shows Phase 6 means EDGE_MULTIUSER=true.
- That decision is not in Option A's "Needed from the user" list (EXEC.md:15992).
- Result: when the admin signs in on live to set up his authenticator with his usual login `edge`, he gets 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS. "Forgot password?" sends nothing for him.

**Why low, not medium**
- **The account works.** As `admin_1` (any case) the sign-in answers 403 MFA_REQUIRED. Setting up the authenticator needs no email (auth_flows.py:408-441).
- **His wrong tries are harmless.** Tries with `edge` match no account, so they do not count towards user #1's limit of 100 failed passwords.
- **The beta is untouched.** A 24 h lock on live does not affect the beta: its sign-in compares against EDGE_LOGIN and EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER and never calls `sign_in_try` (main.py:853-854). The AI, the Monitor and the admin pages are on the beta only.
- **A way back exists for an admin with no email.** The operator unlock is recorded as exactly that (scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py:5-6), and M507 made it work without an authenticator.
- **The lock-out is designed, and the suggested fixes do not prevent it.**
  - Anyone who knows a username can reach the 100-failure limit. This is the NIST limit every account has, not something specific to this account.
  - Adding an email leaves `admin_1` usable as a login, because the lookup matches the username or the email.
  - Keeping `edge` gives a name that is no harder to guess.

**What needs doing:** a decision and a message, not a blocker. Before the switch-on, put the open question (username, email) to the user. Until he decides, tell him his live login is `admin_1`.

confirmed.title: Branch `live` is planned at 13f40871, but that commit's required Backend tests check failed. With checkSuites the live deploy is skipped, or it can only be forced past the K10 a gate
confirmed.fix: Create `live` at aee67c30, whose app tree is byte-identical to 13f40871 apart from the test fix, once that commit's own Backend tests run is green. Record that SHA as the one that goes live and check it in /version. Do not force-deploy a commit with a red check.
confirmed.verifier:
Confirmed, but it is not a blocker.

What holds at 13f40871:
- The test has a race. It reads the marks with no wait, right after `chips.count() == 2`. The page draws them one animation frame later, in a `requestAnimationFrame` inside the `highlightAttached` lifecycle.
- The repository's own record says run 44686714030 (commit 13f40871) failed this test three times in a row, the two TEMPORARY M510 reruns included. I could not read GitHub myself because network calls are off-limits here.
- `backend-tests.yml` runs on every push and has no branch filter, so a new `live` ref runs the same unfixed test again.
- That rerun is not reliably red. The same test file, `test_answer_view.py` and `static/edge-app.js` are unchanged between 99b5ea20 and 13f40871, and run 44677001491 on 99b5ea20 passed every browser test at the first try. So the result is a coin toss, while the commit's red run from the push to main stays on record.

Why this is a real problem whichever way Railway picks its check suites:
- The planned trigger sets `checkSuites` to true, and in this project Railway has already skipped an edge-bff deploy as "CI check suite failed" (655a2e87, M467).
- The user's rule for a push to live (EXEC.md detail 3: "every suite of the beta version must be green") and AGENTS.md K10 a rule out 13f40871.
- So the switch-on as written ("create branch live at the checked commit") is either SKIPPED, or it ships a commit with a red run against the user's rule. That is a deploy that behaves differently than planned.

Why medium and not blocker:
- It fails safe. A skipped deploy exposes nothing to visitors or data.
- The app code of 13f40871 is the same as aee67c30's apart from that one test file.
- The commit that goes live has to be later than 13f40871 anyway. 61d9333b holds the live checker's app fixes (accounts.py, auth_flows.py, config.py, errors.py, main.py, static).
- The working tree's uncommitted EXEC.md "Switch-on order" step 1 already says "the branch `live` at a commit whose own CI run is green (never a red one: the K10 a gate), recorded as the commit that goes live".
- The beta half of the finding does not affect the live site. The beta still runs 99b5ea20, and that code already reads `EDGE_HOUSEKEEPING_ENABLED` (config.py:229), so the planned housekeeping switch still works.

Fix: create `live` at the newest commit that holds the live checker's fixes, once that commit's own Backend tests and other workflow runs are green. Commit that EXEC.md step, and check the deployed commit after the deploy.

confirmed.title: No rollback is written for the first live deployment. Removing edge-bff-live strands its backtest jobs, which blocks user #1's beta Backtest, and once the beta's housekeeping is off nothing purges
confirmed.fix:
Write the rollback into EXEC Option A:
- Turn the beta's housekeeping off only after the live smoke has passed, with the M340 check before that beta redeploy.
- Rollback is three steps:
  1. Remove the live deployment (or its domain).
  2. Set EDGE_HOUSEKEEPING_ENABLED back to true on edge-bff.
  3. Run a reviewed job that ends the live site's open jobs: CANCELLED for site='live' QUEUED rows, FAILED WORKER_LOST for site='live' RUNNING rows.
confirmed.verifier:
Confirmed at 13f40871, with two parts overstated.

**Main defect (confirmed).** User #1 has one owner key on both sites, EDGE_OWNER, because live references the beta's value. The admin holds backtest.run on live: it is a catalog flag and not beta-only, so live_view maps '*' to it. A stopping site never ends its own job. On shutdown the tasks are cancelled and the job stays RUNNING, left for that same site's reap. The beta's reap only touches site='beta' rows, and its claim skips every owner that has a RUNNING row on either site.

So the scenario plays out like this:
1. The live site is removed with `railway down`, the way the probe was. Its first deployment has no earlier EDGE build to fall back to.
2. If user #1 had a live Backtest in flight at that moment, every beta Backtest of user #1 stays QUEUED indefinitely.
3. Cancelling from the beta only sets cancel_requested on the RUNNING row, so it does not help.
4. The beta page polls QUEUED/RUNNING with no timeout and keeps showing "Running…". The beta loop logs nothing, so the lockout is silent for both the admin and the operator.
5. It clears only when a live process runs again, or with a manual database update.

**No rollback written (confirmed).** At 13f40871 and at HEAD 61d9333b, EXEC Option A has no switch-on order and no rollback. RAILWAY_CHANGELOG (aee67c30:28-29) lists "EDGE_HOUSEKEEPING_ENABLED=false on edge-bff" as a switch-on step, not gated on the smoke. CONTRACT 16 (:1316) says to set it false "once edge-bff-live runs". The rollback floors in CONTRACT 17 cover build versions only, and one row even prescribes "edge-bff-live off" without any cleanup. The uncommitted EXEC.md edit in the working tree, which cites this finding, adds a rollback, but it is not in the checked commit.

**Overstated: QUEUE_FULL.** The page keeps one job in flight per tab and cancels it when a newer run starts or the page is left. Three stale QUEUED live rows would need several tabs or API calls. The beta's cancel route has no site filter, so it can end them; I ran it and it worked. The beta page offers no list or button for that, though.

**Overstated: housekeeping.** With housekeeping off on both sites, the impact in pre-launch is low. Registration is closed, there are few outbox and code rows, and an expired session never resolves. The user's 30-day retention rule fails only if the rollback lasts long and nobody turns the switch back on.

**What would have avoided the strand.** Removing only the domain, which keeps the process alive, or running the M340 check before `railway down`. Neither is written down.

**Severity.** Medium, not a blocker. It only bites on a rollback, but at that moment it silently locks the admin out of the beta Backtest.

confirmed.title: Three edge-bff-live references are chains, and the M308 rotation procedure finds only direct consumers. A key rotation at its source leaves the live site on the old key
confirmed.fix: On edge-bff-live, reference the source services directly, as the beta does: ${{terminal-api.TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY}}, ${{backtest-worker.BACKTEST_WORKER_KEY}}, ${{screener-worker.SCREENER_WORKER_KEY}}. Alternatively, make railway_reference_consumers.py follow reference chains (consumers of consumers). Update CONTRACT 16 and the railway.ts block to match.
confirmed.verifier:
The finding stands. I checked it against the code at 13f40871 and ran the repository script offline.

1. **The keys are chained.** On the beta, edge-bff's three keys reference their source services:
   - `TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY = ${{terminal-api.TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY}}`
   - `BACKTEST_WORKER_KEY = ${{backtest-worker...}}`
   - `SCREENER_WORKER_KEY = ${{screener-worker...}}`

   edge-bff-live holds `${{edge-bff.<same name>}}` for each, both in the planned `railway.ts` block and in the values set on Railway (b6ceb5a3). Railway does resolve chained references: `${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}` and `${{market-ai-orc.CATALOG_DATABASE_URL}}`, both templates of other references, are used and work.

2. **The M308 tool lists only direct consumers.** `railway_reference_consumers.py` keeps a variable only when it is exactly one reference and compares it with the requested source pair. It never looks for consumers of consumers, and `--redeploy` redeploys only that list. My offline run with the recorded values:
   - `terminal-api.TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY`, `backtest-worker.BACKTEST_WORKER_KEY` and `screener-worker.SCREENER_WORKER_KEY` each list and redeploy only `['edge-bff']`;
   - edge-bff-live appears only when the source given is `edge-bff.*`.

   AGENTS.md:203 names this script as the rotation procedure. CONTRACT 16 says "one rotation reaches both sites" only for the session secrets, which point straight at edge-bff's own values. No document has a rotation step that names edge-bff-live.

3. **The failure is silent and total for visitors.**
   - terminal-api accepts exactly one gateway key, with no grace for the old one. A stale key gets 401 `proxy_key_rejected`.
   - edge-bff-live turns that into 503 `TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE` for every Terminal call. In pre-launch that is everything a visitor can use (BBCA). The admin's and test accounts' Backtest and Screener fail the same way after a worker-key rotation.
   - `/ready` checks only the database.
   - The `startup_done` marks cover only `EDGE_SESSION_SECRET`, `EDGE_CODE_SECRET` and `EDGE_MFA_KEY`, not these three keys.
   - The site redeploys only on a push to the `live` branch, so nothing heals the stale key. This kind of stale reference already went unnoticed for 13 days (M308) and 5 days (the audit-store entry).

**What could soften it, and why I did not refute on it.** On the 2026-11-16 rotation, Railway itself started a deployment of the direct consumer, because the variable was set without `--skip-deploys`. Whether Railway also starts one for a consumer two links down is recorded nowhere, and I could not test it offline. It does not happen at all when a key is set with `--skip-deploys`, the repository's usual way of setting secrets, or through the dashboard. In those cases the script is the only thing that redeploys consumers.

**Why medium.** It is not a switch-on blocker: the switch-on involves no rotation. It needs a key rotation while the live site runs, for example after a leak like M464. When that happens, the live Terminal goes down silently. The fix is cheap before the `railway.ts` block is declared: reference the source services directly on edge-bff-live, or make the script follow chains.

**Same gap, smaller impact.** `BACKTEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and `BACKTEST_MAX_RESULT_BYTES` (not secrets) are chained the same way.

confirmed.verifier:
The finding holds. I checked it in the code at 13f40871 and with a local run.

1. **The planned switch-on leaves the email mode at log.**
   - The live settings are log mode with EDGE_EMAIL_LOG_ALLOWED=true, justified as "until the Resend key: CONTRACT 16, no one registers in pre-launch".
   - The "Still to do at the switch-on" list has no email step: the branch, the GitHub source, beta housekeeping off, railway.ts. The same is true at HEAD 61d9333b and in the uncommitted EXEC "Switch-on order" in the working tree.
   - The live site would only send email if someone sets EDGE_EMAIL_MODE=resend and EDGE_EMAIL_FROM. The sender looks only at the mode, so a RESEND_API_KEY entered in the dashboard on its own changes nothing. No step records doing this for edge-bff-live.
   - The only written Resend step is in Phase 1, for the beta. Its webhook URL is edge-bff-dev, which answers 404 to the hook while the switch is off.

2. **This goes against the user's recorded conditions.**
   - "Ok kita tunggu 1-3": the website code goes on edge-bff-live only after Resend is ready.
   - Test accounts set their passwords through "Forgot password" (needs Resend). This is in EXEC, in CONTRACT 17 and in guest.md.
   - Option A lists the Resend key among what is needed from the user. Only the upgrade contact "may follow".
   - CONTRACT 16 does allow log mode "for a test before its Resend key", and the plan relies on that. But it does not settle the conflict with CONTRACT 17 and the user's words.

3. **In log mode no test account can set its first password.**
   - edge_test_account.py gives each new account a random verifier that no password matches.
   - "Forgot password" stays open in pre-launch and queues the reset code inside the email payload.
   - In log mode the sender sends nothing. It marks the row sent with provider 'log' and keeps the payload. The code is masked in the log and works for 5 minutes.
   - No script reads a code out of the outbox. The only mention is mailer.py's note about a "dev tester".
   - A workaround would mean an operator job printing a live reset code to the Railway logs within its 5 minutes. That breaks the secret-redaction rule.

**Impact:** if the switch-on follows the recorded steps, the admin (MFA enrolment needs no email) and visitors work. Every test account stays locked out, so the plans cannot be tried as Option A intends.

**Severity: medium.** There is no security impact, and the fix is settings only: the user enters the Resend key; set EDGE_EMAIL_FROM and EDGE_EMAIL_MODE=resend; remove EDGE_EMAIL_LOG_ALLOWED; add the webhook to app.edgefinance.id once the site is open. confirmed.title: On live, user #1 signs in only as `admin_1` and has no email. The item recorded as "to decide before EDGE_MULTIUSER is switched on" is missing from Option A
confirmed.fix: Before the switch-on, put the decision to the user with context: keep `admin_1` (and state it in the smoke steps) or choose another username. Add the admin's email through a reviewed, audited statement so a reset way back exists. Add both items to Option A's list.
confirmed.verifier:
Not refuted, but the severity should be low, not medium.

What is confirmed:
- EXEC.md:15591-15594 says the user must choose the admin's username and add an email before EDGE_MULTIUSER is switched on. ERRORS M478 (10071-10072) says "to be decided before Phase 6". No later record closes this.
- Option A's list of what is needed from the user (EXEC.md:15992-15993) leaves it out.
- On live, user #1 is `admin_1` with no email. `edge` is reserved in the code and in a database CHECK.
- So at the switch-on, the admin's beta login `edge` gets 401 on live. There is no self-service way back from a password lock or a forgotten live password: no email, and no route to change the email.
- My own test on a clean export of 13f40871 shows every mechanical claim.

What is overstated:
1. The missing email does not cause the stranger lockout. Any account can be locked this fast, email or not. From one address, staying under the 10-per-15-minutes limit, it takes 2.5 h. After the 24 h lock ends, 10 more tries lock it again. A reset only sets the count to 0. The user accepted this 100-failure lock with "2a" on 2026-11-20 (EXEC.md:16152). The email only changes who lifts the lock.
2. The beta is not affected. Its switch-off sign-in never reads the lock (main.py:849-854). The beta answered 200 during the lock.
3. The operator unlock is the designed way back for an admin without an email (scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py:5-6, fixed by M507 C3-18). It worked in my test.
4. On live the admin sees only the masked site (no admin routes, no AI), so a lock costs it only the live view. Guests and test accounts are not affected.
5. `admin_1` is documented (README.md:897-899, EXEC.md:15711), and signing in as `admin_1` with MFA works.

So this is a missing checklist item and a user decision to put on the list, not a code or security defect. The switch-on is safe without it.

One more point: an address can belong to only one account (users_email_one_account). If the user gives their address to a test account, the admin cannot have it. So ask for the admin's email together with the test accounts' addresses.

Small citation slip: the failure cap is at accounts.py:47, not :44.
